newsitem.title: USA: N.J. governor wants deputy treasurer for top spot.
newsitem.headline: N.J. governor wants deputy treasurer for top spot.

text.p: New Jersey Gov. Christie Whitman on Monday said she intended to nominate James DiEleuterio, the deputy state treasurer, to replace Brian Clymer as treasurer.
Clymer plans to leave state government on July 1.
DiEleuterio started working for the state government in 1971 as an auditor intern in the Division of Taxation.
"Jim DiEleuterio earned his stripes in the trenches," Whitman said in prepared remarks.

Later, the governor praised his understanding of the issues confronting the state. "Jim DiEleuterio has always been willing to tackle tough issues and to commit all of the time and energy necessary to get the job done right," Whitman said.
DiEleuterio, a 1979 graduate of Rider University, earned his Masters in Business Administration from Widener University in 1987.
He also has served as assistant director of the New Jersey Division of Taxation and assistant state treasurer for tax policy.
